variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Replication stores copies of the same data on multiple nodes. It improves availability, durability, and sometimes read capacity. Partitioning divides a dataset into non-overlapping pieces. Sharding usually means placing those partitions on independently scalable nodes.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Replication
pairs.detail: Use replicas to survive node or zone loss, serve permitted reads closer to clients, and recover from a failed copy.
pairs.explanation: Use replicas to survive node or zone loss, serve permitted reads closer to clients, and recover from a failed copy. The write protocol must decide which replicas acknowledge a commit and how lagging copies converge.

pairs.label: Sharding
pairs.detail: Use shards when one node cannot hold the bytes or process the write workload.
pairs.explanation: Use shards when one node cannot hold the bytes or process the write workload. The routing layer must map every key to exactly one current owner and handle queries that span owners.

variants.hint:
Replication: Use replicas to survive node or zone loss, serve permitted reads closer to clients, and recover from a failed copy.

Sharding: Use shards when one node cannot hold the bytes or process the write workload.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

pairs.label: Hash partitioning
pairs.detail: A stable hash spreads many independent keys well.
pairs.explanation: A stable hash spreads many independent keys well. Point routing is direct, but ordered range scans scatter. Plain hash(key) mod N moves many keys when N changes; virtual buckets, consistent hashing, or a directory reduce movement.

pairs.label: Range partitioning
pairs.detail: Contiguous ranges keep ordered scans local and can split at explicit boundaries.
pairs.explanation: Contiguous ranges keep ordered scans local and can split at explicit boundaries. Uneven value growth and append-heavy keys create active ranges that must split before they saturate.

pairs.label: Directory partitioning
pairs.detail: A directory maps a tenant, bucket, or range to an owner.
pairs.explanation: A directory maps a tenant, bucket, or range to an owner. Placement and migration are flexible, but the directory becomes critical metadata that needs versioning, caching, availability, and atomic updates.

variants.hint:
Hash partitioning: A stable hash spreads many independent keys well.

Range partitioning: Contiguous ranges keep ordered scans local and can split at explicit boundaries.

Directory partitioning: A directory maps a tenant, bucket, or range to an owner.

pairs.label: Copy a snapshot
pairs.detail: Copy a consistent base image to the destination and record the source log position.
pairs.explanation: Copy a consistent base image to the destination and record the source log position. Keep normal reads and writes on the source.

pairs.label: Catch up changes
pairs.detail: Stream mutations after the snapshot position until destination lag is inside a small, measured cutover budget.
pairs.explanation: Stream mutations after the snapshot position until destination lag is inside a small, measured cutover budget.

pairs.label: Fence and cut over
pairs.detail: Prevent stale writers, atomically publish the new directory epoch, and make routers reject or refresh older ownership metadata.
pairs.explanation: Prevent stale writers, atomically publish the new directory epoch, and make routers reject or refresh older ownership metadata.

pairs.label: Verify, then clean
pairs.detail: Compare counts, checksums, and sampled reads.
pairs.explanation: Compare counts, checksums, and sampled reads. Retain the source through a rollback window before deleting old copies.

pairs.label: Replica loss
pairs.detail: Stop routing to the failed member, verify the remaining acknowledgement threshold, replace the copy, and stream or repair missing history.
pairs.explanation: Stop routing to the failed member, verify the remaining acknowledgement threshold, replace the copy, and stream or repair missing history. Capacity must support foreground traffic with one member absent.

pairs.label: Primary loss
pairs.detail: Fence the old primary before promoting a caught-up replica.
pairs.explanation: Fence the old primary before promoting a caught-up replica. Publish a higher topology epoch, refresh routers, and make retries idempotent. Otherwise a partitioned old primary can create split brain.

pairs.label: Shard data loss
pairs.detail: Restore that shard from backup and replay durable logs.
pairs.explanation: Restore that shard from backup and replay durable logs. Replicas are not backups: accidental deletes, corruption, and bad application writes can replicate to every copy.

Replica loss: Stop routing to the failed member, verify the remaining acknowledgement threshold, replace the copy, and stream or repair missing history.

Primary loss: Fence the old primary before promoting a caught-up replica.

Shard data loss: Restore that shard from backup and replay durable logs.

variants.prompt: Which statement correctly separates replication from sharding?
options: Replication divides keys among owners, while sharding stores copies of each key
